title: Non-blocking follow-ups from PR #121 review (api-stocks-indicator-history-followups)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #121 (api-stocks-indicator-history-followups, the analyse_history() O(range_size x history_length) -> O(history_length) fix), tracked here so they aren't lost once that PR merges and its comments scroll out of view.

checklist.step: backend/app/signals/engine.py:521 -- analyse_history() now calls drop_malformed_daily_bars(daily_ohlcv) once at the top (added so the precomputed indicator series and every per-bar truncated slice agree on which rows exist). This is a genuine, currently-dormant behavior change versus the pre-PR implementation for a caller that passes a not-fully-cleaned daily_ohlcv with a malformed bar in the *middle* of history (not just the trailing bar): the malformed bar's date is now silently omitted from the returned history list entirely, whereas the pre-PR implementation still emitted an entry for that date (with indicator/signal values effectively duplicating the prior clean bar's, since analyse() re-cleaned its own truncated slice internally either way). Reproduced directly: with a 60-row synthetic daily frame with row 30's close set to NaN, the pre-PR analyse_history() returned 60 entries (including one dated at the malformed row, matching the prior clean bar's values) while this PR's analyse_history() returns 59 entries (that date entirely absent). The only real caller (app/api/routers/stocks.py) already calls drop_malformed_daily_bars before invoking analyse_history, so this has no live production effect today, and arguably the new behavior is more correct (no chart point for a day whose data never really arrived) -- but it's undocumented (no decisions entry or docstring note acknowledging the change from the prior contract) and untested (no regression test exercises analyse_history() with a malformed bar mixed into history rather than pre-cleaned/trailing-only). Add a regression test for this case and either document the behavior change explicitly (docstring + a decisions entry) or, if judged unintentional/undesirable, reconcile it with the pre-PR emit-an-entry-anyway behavior.

backend/app/signals/engine.py:354-355 -- the docstring/decisions entry's claim that this PR turns analyse_history()'s cost from O(range_size x history_length) into O(history_length) total is not strictly accurate: elder_bull_power(daily_ohlcv['high'], ema_13) / elder_bear_power(daily_ohlcv['low'], ema_13) (a vectorized High/Low - EMA(13) subtraction) are computed fresh over each bar's own full truncated slice inside analyse() every call, not precomputed once over the full series and sliced like the five daily + three weekly indicators this PR did precompute -- so this remains an O(i)-per-bar cost, on top of the already-acknowledged (in the PR's own decisions entry) per-bar volume-rolling-average and _weekly_through_bar_date boolean-mask costs. The function's true worst-case asymptotic complexity is therefore still O(range_size x history_length), just with a much smaller constant (the dominant terms removed). Confirmed empirically this doesn't matter in practice for realistic history lengths -- a synthetic worst-case benchmark (a choppy/oscillating bullish-tide series engineered to trigger the Wave screen's oversold/Force-Index-spike path -- the other real per-bar-recompute-shaped cost, _is_force_index_spike's rolling-std -- far more often than typical market data) still showed clean linear scaling from n=500 to n=4000 (0.53s/1.01s/2.06s/4.04s), matching the PR's own reported linear-to-5000-bars scaling. This is a documentation-precision nit, not a live performance bug -- either qualify the O(history_length) framing more precisely (e.g. note the residual O(n) terms and why they don't matter in practice) or extend the same precompute-and-slice pattern to elder_bull_power/elder_bear_power for full consistency/asymptotic correctness.

backend/app/signals/triple_screen.py:214-220 (_is_force_index_spike) -- pinpoints the same residual-complexity gap as the checklist item above, from a second independent review pass (the code-review skill), with a concrete failure scenario: force_index_2ema.rolling(window=13).std() computes the rolling std over the *entire* slice it's handed (not just the trailing ~13 bars needed) before taking .iloc[-1], so this call is O(len(slice)) rather than O(1). Since _wave_lookback can invoke evaluate_wave (and transitively this function, whenever the Stochastic-threshold condition is already met) up to 6 times per bar across analyse_history()'s full range, a ticker/date-range where Wave crosses OVERSOLD_PULLBACK/OVERBOUGHT_RALLY often enough to hit this branch repeatedly could still see close-to-quadratic total cost for GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators?range=max, despite the rest of this PR reducing everything else to O(n). Empirically this doesn't bite in practice: a worst-case-engineered benchmark (an oscillating bullish-tide series with volume spikes, deliberately maximizing how often the oversold+spike branch fires) still scaled linearly from n=500 to n=4000 during this review -- but the PR's own decisions-entry benchmark only tested synthetic data that likely didn't exercise this threshold-crossing-heavy path either, so the O(history_length) claim remains unverified for the adversarial case in the wild. Lowest-effort fix: slice force_index_2ema to its trailing _FORCE_INDEX_SPIKE_WINDOW bars (`force_index_2ema.iloc[-_FORCE_INDEX_SPIKE_WINDOW:]`) before calling .rolling(...).std(), turning this into genuine O(1) work per call regardless of how large the slice handed in is.

decisions.decision: For item 1 (the dormant mid-history-malformed-bar behavior change), kept the current (post-PR-#121) behavior -- a malformed bar mid-history is entirely omitted from analyse_history()'s output -- rather than reconciling it back to the pre-PR duplicate-entry behavior, and documented it explicitly in analyse_history()'s own docstring plus added a regression test (TestAnalyseHistory.test_malformed_bar_mid_history_is_dropped_from_history_entirely) that pins down the current behavior (one fewer entry, malformed date absent).
decisions.rationale: Confirmed via a standalone script loading the pre-PR engine.py (git show 2f82721:backend/app/signals/engine.py) side-by-side with the current module on the same 60-row synthetic frame with row 30 malformed: pre-PR analyse_history() returned 60 entries including one for the malformed date whose SignalResult was identical to the prior clean bar's (signal/confidence/indicators/screens all equal), while the current implementation returns 59 entries with that date entirely absent -- exactly matching the checklist item's own reproduction. The only real caller (app.api.routers.stocks.get_indicator_history) always pre-cleans daily_ohlcv before calling analyse_history, so neither behavior is reachable in production today, and 'no chart point for a day whose data never really arrived' is a more honest contract for any future caller than silently duplicating the prior bar's values under that date -- reverting to the pre-PR behavior would mean re-introducing a phantom duplicate-value entry with no real upside. Documented instead of silently leaving it to be reverse-engineered from the diff, per the checklist item's own explicit ask.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Reconciling to the pre-PR emit-an-entry-anyway behavior (re-inserting a duplicate entry for the malformed date) was considered and rejected -- it would require analyse_history() to special-case a bar it just decided to treat as unfit for computation, adding real code complexity to restore a behavior that was itself somewhat accidental (a byproduct of analyse() re-cleaning its own slice, not an intentional design), for a code path with no live caller today.

decisions.decision: For item 2, qualified the O(history_length) performance claim in analyse_history()'s docstring rather than extending the precompute-and-slice pattern to elder_bull_power/elder_bear_power.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item itself already reports empirical confirmation (synthetic worst-case benchmark, linear scaling to n=4000) that the residual O(n)-per-bar cost from elder_bull_power/elder_bear_power (plus the already-acknowledged volume-rolling-average and _weekly_through_bar_date costs) doesn't matter in practice for realistic history lengths -- this is a documentation-precision nit, not a live performance bug, exactly as the checklist item frames it. Extending the precompute pattern further would add real code complexity (two more optional keyword parameters threaded through analyse()/elder_bull_power/elder_bear_power) to fix an asymptotic-complexity claim's wording rather than any observed latency problem.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Extending elder_bull_power/elder_bear_power into the same precompute-and-slice pattern as the five daily + three weekly indicators was considered (the checklist item offers it as an alternative) but rejected as unnecessary complexity for a cost that's empirically negligible -- consistent with the api-stocks-indicator-history-followups task's own prior decision not to further optimize the volume-rolling-average/_weekly_through_bar_date costs for the same reason.

decisions.decision: For item 3, applied the checklist item's own suggested one-line fix (slice force_index_2ema to its trailing _FORCE_INDEX_SPIKE_WINDOW bars before .rolling(...).std()) in backend/app/signals/triple_screen.py's _is_force_index_spike.
decisions.rationale: A rolling standard deviation at a fixed position depends only on its own trailing window, never on rows outside it, so pre-slicing to the trailing window before calling .rolling(window=...).std().iloc[-1] cannot change the computed value -- only the amount of work pandas does to reach it. Verified this directly: (1) a standalone script comparing the old (full-slice) and new (trailing-window-sliced) implementations of _is_force_index_spike across every prefix length 1..500 of a synthetic Force Index series, both directions (negative=True/False) -- zero mismatches across 1000 checks; (2) end-to-end via analyse_history() on a 300-bar synthetic series engineered to oscillate (maximizing how often the Wave screen's oversold/Force-Index-spike branch fires, the same adversarial shape the checklist item's own benchmark used) -- a SHA-256 digest of every bar's (date, signal, confidence, wave state) across the full 300-bar history was byte-for-byte identical before and after the fix (comparing against the pre-fix triple_screen.py loaded from git HEAD). Also reran the full backend test suite (571 passed, including the existing Screen 2/Wave and Force-Index-spike tests) and confirmed 100% coverage on both touched modules.
decisions.alternatives_considered: None -- the checklist item already specified the exact one-line fix, and it's the lowest-risk option (no change to any other call site, no new parameter).
